# Per-service test floors for the Spring Boot 4.x migration wave.
#
# WHY: a migration that quietly deletes or disables tests looks identical to a clean one — the suite
# still goes green, it just proves less. The zero-tests guard catches a suite that vanished entirely;
# this file catches the far more likely case of a suite that SHRANK.
#
# THE NUMBERS ARE SUREFIRE EXECUTION COUNTS, NOT GREP COUNTS.
# The first version of this file used the anchored grep '^\s*@(Test|ParameterizedTest)\b' and was
# WRONG on every service by exactly 10: each service has 4 @ParameterizedTest methods that expand to
# 14 executions, and grep counts declarations while surefire counts executions. A floor set from grep
# sits 10 below reality, so a migration could delete ten real tests and still pass the gate — the
# gate would have been vacuous in precisely the direction it exists to prevent.
# This is the trap testing.md already warns about: the final source of truth is the surefire summary
# of a real run, never a grep. Measured on Boot 3.5.16 at f7e549c.
#
# RULE: the executed test count per service must be >= the floor. A DECREASE is a blocking finding
# and requires a per-test written justification at the gate — never a silent floor edit. Raising a
# floor after adding tests is expected and welcome; re-measure with surefire, do not grep.
#
# format: <service> <minimum executed tests>
user 97
product 99
cart 85
order 115
payment 84
